name: Amides, C8-18 and C18-unsaturated, N-(hydroxyethyl)
description: Amides, C8-18 and C18-unsaturated, N-(hydroxyethyl) , also identified by CAS 69227-24-3 , is commercially known as Cocamide MEA. This coconut-derived fatty acid monoethanolamide is used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. It functions primarily as a foam booster, thickener, and emulsifier, improving the performance and texture of surfactant-based systems. In shampoos, body washes, and liquid soaps, it thickens the base formulation effectively. The compound stabilizes foam generated by primary surfactants such as sodium lauryl sulfate. Home care and industrial cleaners rely on it to boost detergency and maintain foam structure across a range of pH conditions. Textile processing operations use it as an emulsifier and dispersing agent in scouring and finishing baths. In these environments, consistent emulsification of oils and waxes is critical for high-quality production results. In paper manufacturing, it supports sizing formulations and improves surface treatment uniformity. Cocamide MEA is supplied as a solid flake or waxy solid at ambient temperature, typically requiring mild heating for handling. It is available in cosmetic-grade and industrial-grade specifications for various needs. Cosmetic grades conform to standards relevant for leave-on and rinse-off personal care applications to ensure safety and efficacy. Drum and bulk quantities are standard supply formats for industrial buyers seeking reliable chemical sourcing. This versatile ingredient remains a staple for manufacturers requiring robust foam stabilization and viscosity control.
